triggers.prompt: I signed in with my other Claude account and now the sidebar is almost empty. Where did all my conversations go?
triggers.expected: Fires, explains that the transcripts are intact and only the per-account index is partitioned, and offers the union.

triggers.prompt: 换了个账号登录，session 全没了
Can my two accounts on this machine share the same conversation list?
triggers.expected: Fires, and reports what would be copied before writing anything.

triggers.prompt: 帮我找回以前那些对话，侧边栏现在只剩几条了
triggers.expected: Fires on a second Chinese phrasing, not only the one the description spells out first.

triggers.prompt: I renamed a bunch of conversations under one account but my other account still shows the old titles.
triggers.expected: Fires; title reconciliation across account indexes is part of what it does.

non_triggers.prompt: Rename these conversations onto the dated scheme.
non_triggers.expected: Does not fire; naming conversations is a different skill.

non_triggers.prompt: Delete last month's conversations, they are cluttering the sidebar.
non_triggers.expected: Does not fire. It only ever adds index entries and never removes a conversation.

non_triggers.prompt: Move my Claude history over to my new laptop.
non_triggers.expected: Does not fire; it unions indexes on one machine and does not transfer history between machines.

behaviors.prompt: Merge my session lists across accounts. There are three account indexes on this machine holding 36, 358 and 81 conversations.
expectations: Runs the report first and shows the plan — how many entries would be copied and how much disk they add — before writing anything.
Does not pass --apply until the plan has been put to the user.
Names which org subdirectory each account's copies land in rather than writing to an arbitrary one.

behaviors.prompt: I logged into my work account and every conversation from my personal account is gone. Can you get them back?
expectations: Corrects the premise: the transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/ carry no account field and were never deleted, only the sidebar index is per-account.
Mentions that claude --resume in a terminal already lists all of them, which is the answer if only one old conversation is needed.
Offers the union as the fix for the sidebar rather than describing it as recovery.

behaviors.prompt: The merge left duplicate-looking rows in my sidebar. Delete the ones from the old account.
expectations: Does not delete conversations or index entries to tidy the list.
Offers --undo, which removes exactly what a previous --apply wrote, as the only removal it performs.

behaviors.prompt: Apply the session merge for me, I have already seen the plan.
expectations: States that the sidebar is unchanged until the desktop app restarts, because the app reads this index at startup and does not rescan while running.
Flags that restarting interrupts conversations that are still running, and leaves the timing to the user.
Says the run is recorded and reversible with --undo.

behaviors.prompt: The naming sweep renamed 40 conversations while I was signed in as my personal account. I just switched to my work account and they still show the old names.
expectations: Explains that a rename writes one index file, so the other accounts' copies still hold the old name, and that copying alone cannot fix it because the entry is already present.
Runs reunite, which reconciles the diverged titles as part of its normal pass, rather than proposing a fresh renaming run under the second account.
Notes that the reconciled titles are recorded and that --undo puts them back.
